cells.tense: You're keeping what the change left standing, and you know it's you doing the keeping — nothing in your hands right now is accidental.
cells.ask: Offer one piece of what you're holding to someone else, and let what they hand back become part of it.
cells.core:
You're the one keeping what the change left standing, and you know it's you doing the keeping. Nothing in your hands right now is accidental — you picked it, sorted it, held it. This is reading a room by its shapes: who's circling what, which pattern is about to tip, what a structure can and can't carry. You can see how a thing works without needing to own every piece of it, and that isn't distance. It's the reason your keeping is clean.

What's free to feed this next is exchange. Someone hands you something and you hand back, and the shape changes without losing anything — the way a good conversation leaves you holding more than you brought. You don't have to work out whether it's fair. You'll feel it when it is, and that feeling is enough to move on.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one keeping what survived the change, and you know it's yours to keep.

cells.tense: You're holding on ahead of the change — gripping a shape that hasn't arrived yet, bracing the pattern against a future that won't match.
cells.ask: Leave one thing you're holding unresolved for a day, and feel what wants to come toward you before you've decided its shape.
cells.core:
You're gripping the shape ahead of the change. Watching the pattern, checking it, holding it against a future that hasn't shown up yet — and the holding is now the work, not the thing held. What you're protecting hasn't been threatened. You've just been standing guard since before anyone asked.

When this flows right, an ending lands and you let it land — no rush to pin the new shape down before it's ready, no need to see the final form first. You trusted the settling and it held, and other people felt steadier standing near you. That's still available. Feel for the shape arriving on its own, wanting to be met rather than forced — and meeting it is what lets you put the guard down.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed behind you — holding a shape you already set down, watching a pattern you already stopped steering.
cells.ask: Pick one direction that came from how you actually feel, and move on it today — not toward a plan, toward what's pulling you.
cells.core:
You're still at the door that's already closed behind you. Holding a shape you already set down, watching a pattern you already stopped steering. The seeing still works — you can still make out how the thing was made — but the hand that was keeping it isn't in the room anymore, and the watching has turned into standing still.

Working right, this reads the shape of a thing and lets it go, because the reading was for moving, not for keeping. The pattern told you which way to step, and stepping was the point. That flow comes back by moving, not by watching — something you feel right now can point you, and the pointing is what makes a direction real. You don't need the whole shape. You need the next step that's already pulling, taken while it pulls.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped holding it, but you haven't stopped watching it.

cells.tense: You're already holding the shape of this — you're the one keeping it steady in the room — and you're talking like the pattern was just there for anyone to see.
cells.ask: Say out loud that one shape you keep steady is yours to keep — the naming is the part you've been leaving out.
cells.core:
You're already keeping the shape of this. People keep things steady because you're the one holding them — and you talk about the pattern like it just showed up, as if anyone could see it. The holding is real. The claim that it's yours isn't made yet.

Structure that serves what it organizes doesn't announce itself. It's just there, clear and reliable, and things make sense around it — people bring you the tangled thing because of how you hold it. Name one shape you've been keeping without saying so. Say it plain, out loud, once. That sentence turns the holding from a background into something someone can actually stand on — including you.
